strengths: The paper proposes a well-motivated architectural decoupling of scene representation (viewpoint tokens) from input images, addressing a real scalability bottleneck in feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction methods that rely on full multi-view attention.

The two-stage attention scheme (per-view cross-attention + viewpoint self-attention) is a sensible and effective way to reduce quadratic complexity while retaining global multi-view consistency, and the FLOPs/memory/time analysis (Tab. 6, Appendix F) substantiates the claimed efficiency gains.

Extensive experiments across RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID (cross-dataset generalization), with multiple viewpoint/resolution configurations, consistently show state-of-the-art or near-SOTA PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS while using substantially fewer Gaussians and less compute/memory than strong baselines (GS-LRM, DepthSplat, MVSplat, pixelSplat, LongLRM).

Thorough ablation studies (number of layers, iterative refinement, resolution decoupling, token uplifting, self-attention necessity, group-attention alternative, initialization schemes) support the individual design choices rather than just the overall pipeline.

The wide-coverage comparison against optimization-based methods (3D-GS, Mip-Splatting) and LongLRM, including a fine-tuning variant, is a nice demonstration that feed-forward reconstruction can approach or exceed per-scene optimization quality at a fraction of the time.
The paper is clearly written, well organized, and provides substantial supplementary detail (implementation, additional ablations, qualitative figures) supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The 'iterative refinement' framing as analogous to gradient-based optimization is more a conceptual/motivational narrative than a rigorously established equivalence; the ablation (single cross-attention layer + many self-attention layers) shows that repeated cross-attention helps, but doesn't strongly validate the optimizer analogy itself, which is largely rhetorical.

Self-attention across all viewpoint tokens is still, by the authors' own admission in Limitations, a bottleneck that will not scale indefinitely with view count; the largest demonstrated view count (32) is still moderate for 'wide-coverage' scenes, and no truly large-N (e.g., 100+) scaling experiment is shown beyond the DL3DV 12-view OOM comparison against DepthSplat.

The comparisons against GS-LRM and some other baselines are asterisked as reproduced without official code/pretrained models (Table 1), leaving some reliance on numbers copied from other papers rather than direct reproduction, which slightly weakens the rigor of comparison.

The method still fundamentally requires known/accurate camera poses (acknowledged as a limitation), restricting applicability relative to recent pose-free feed-forward approaches, and no experiments address this limitation empirically.

Some design choices (e.g., patch size, k=2 expansion factor for uplifting, choice of mini-batch cross-attention variant used for main results vs. MC variants) are set empirically without deeper justification or sensitivity analysis beyond a few ablation tables.

The paper does not report variance/multiple seeds or statistical significance for the reported metrics, which is common in this literature but limits certainty about the size of the sometimes small quality gaps (e.g., LPIPS differences of 0.01-0.02) relative to strongest baselines in some settings.

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important problem: scalability of feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction models with respect to number of views and image resolution.

The core idea of decoupling the Gaussian/scene representation from input image resolution via compact viewpoint tokens, combined with a two-stage (cross-attention then self-attention) interaction scheme, is a sensible and reasonably novel architectural contribution that meaningfully reduces the quadratic attention cost of prior full-attention approaches (e.g., GS-LRM).

Extensive and fairly rigorous experimental evaluation: results on RE10K, DL3DV (multiple resolutions/view counts), cross-dataset generalization to ACID, wide-baseline/zero-shot tests on Tanks&Temples and Mip-NeRF360, depth/geometry evaluation against pseudo-depth and point clouds, robustness to pose noise, and post-prediction optimization comparisons.

Thorough ablation studies (model depth, resolution decoupling, token uplifting, mini-batch cross-attention variants, initialization strategies, group- vs per-view attention) that support the design choices individually.

Strong reported efficiency-quality trade-off: fewer parameters and Gaussians than baselines while achieving competitive or superior PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, notably faster inference (0.5s vs ~8min for optimization-based 3D-GS) and better scaling to more views/higher resolution than DepthSplat/Long-LRM.

The attention visualization (Fig. 8/18) provides some interpretability into the claimed 'iterative refinement' behavior, showing attended tokens converging to geometrically consistent regions across layers.
Good reproducibility support: detailed architectural and training hyperparameters, FLOPs analysis, and supplementary implementation details are provided.
weaknesses: The individual architectural components (Perceiver-style cross-attention/self-attention decomposition, mini-batch/token-subsampling for attention, Plücker ray embeddings, iterative refinement framing) are each adapted from existing works (Perceiver, VGGT's alternating attention, prior LRM works); the novelty lies primarily in combining these ideas for 3D Gaussian reconstruction rather than introducing a fundamentally new mechanism, which somewhat limits originality.

The 'iterative refinement as optimization' framing (analogy to gradient descent) is more of a conceptual narrative than a formally justified claim; no explicit loss/energy function is optimized at each layer, so the analogy, while illustrative, is not rigorously established.

Baseline comparisons, while broad, are largely against a limited set of recent feed-forward methods (MVSplat, DepthSplat, Gen-Den, Long-LRM); some very recent strong pixel-aligned or pose-free baselines (e.g., VGGT-based reconstruction methods) are only cited but not directly compared quantitatively.

The paper acknowledges reliance on accurate camera poses as a limitation, and the self-attention bottleneck across viewpoint tokens remains a scalability concern for very large numbers of views (e.g., Table 15 still shows non-trivial runtime growth, though no OOM).

Some ablations (e.g., Table 9's random/group-attention/init variants) are run only under a single, relatively small configuration (4 views, half resolution), which may not fully generalize to the paper's headline high-resolution/wide-coverage settings.

The quantitative gains over the strongest baseline (DepthSplat) on RE10K/DL3DV are sometimes modest (e.g., PSNR differences within ~1 dB in several settings), and improvements partly stem from using more input views or additional held-out supervision setups, which somewhat complicates head-to-head comparison fairness across differing view counts.

Presentation clarity could be improved in places: the interpretation section's gradient-descent notation is dense and not fully self-contained, and some table settings (e.g., MC variants, H/F/Q resolution codes) require cross-referencing multiple sections to parse.
